J2.evidence: «لا تَكْسَعِ الشَّوْلَ بِأَغْبَارِهَا»: in the lexicons كسع الناقة بغبرها = to leave the remnant milk in the udder (not milking it out, splashing cold water to make it recede). EN 'Do not leave the dry she-camels with the remnants of their milk unmilked' conveys that sense correctly; the reviewer's cold-water gloss is the mechanism of the same act, not a different meaning.

J1.evidence: «لا تَكْسَعِ الشَّوْلَ بِأَغْبَارِهَا»: in the lexicons كسع الناقة بغبرها means leaving the remnant milk in the udder (not milking it out) so the camel stays strong. The proverb tells you to milk it out because you do not know who will get their young. EN 'Do not leave the dry she-camels with the remnants of their milk unmilked; you do not know who will deliver their young' is accurate, and the source itself glosses «الأغبار: بقايا اللبن». The cold-water sense is one gloss of كسع, but the EN reading is correct.

J2.evidence: Text «قال عبدالله بن عباس: إلاَّ ثلاث آيات، نزلْنَ بين مكة والمدينة ... فأنزل الله ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُم فعَاقِبُوا﴾ إلى آخر ثلاث آيات» is the Meccan/Medinan note of Surat al-Nahl (16:126-128 exception), not about 15:99 or any ayah of surah 15; no correct range exists within this surah, so placement needs a cross-surah decision.

J1.evidence: Ibn Abbas: «إلاَّ ثلاث آيات، نزلْنَ بين مكة والمدينة ... فأنزل الله ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُم فعَاقِبُوا﴾ إلى آخر ثلاث آيات» is the Meccan/Medinan note on Surat al-Nahl (16:126-128). It has nothing to do with 15:99 «وَٱعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَكَ ٱلْيَقِينُ» or any ayah of surah 15, so there is no correct range in this surah. It is source text misattached to the end of al-Hijr.
